note: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed.

items.title: Jamestown
items.text: English settlers established Jamestown in 1607 on the James River, within Powhatan country. Its coastal location connected the settlement to Atlantic shipping.

items.title: Plymouth
items.text: The land that became Plymouth Colony was Wampanoag land. The point locates Plymouth rather than outlining either Indigenous territory or a colonial claim.

items.title: Philadelphia
items.text: In 1776 the Declaration of Independence announced separation from Britain. Philadelphia is the location of the congressional decision, not a frontier between armies.

items.title: Original states
items.text: The Treaty of Paris of 1783 named the thirteen states and recognised US independence. British recognition was a diplomatic act; it did not obtain Indigenous consent to the treaty’s western claims.
